clue.text: Heavenly nymphs a year in Pluto's realm

indicators.note: the year sits inside the god's underworld kingdom, so one piece is put within the other

parts.note: Pluto ruled the underworld, known as Hades
Y is the standard abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: Celestial nymphs spend a year in the underworld kingdom of Pluto.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hyades were nymphs of Greek myth placed in the sky as a star cluster, hence 'heavenly'.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth these daughters of Atlas became a star cluster in Taurus, so they are nymphs set among the stars.

clue.text: The wreck of this heavenly body

definitions.text: The wreck of this heavenly body

parts.words: The wreck of this heavenly body
parts.note: recalls Longfellow's poem about a shipwrecked schooner named after the evening star

explanation.surface: A star or planet has been wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: Longfellow's poem 'The Wreck of the Hesperus' names a ship after the evening star; the clue reads like a cosmic disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: The evening star in classical naming, and also the doomed schooner of a famous poem.

clue.text: Like Venus in the Louvre, toplessly innocuous

indicators.note: without its top, so the first letter of the word for innocuous is dropped

parts.note: innocuous means harmless, doing no damage

explanation.surface: The famous statue in the Paris gallery is described as bare-chested and inoffensive.
explanation.walkthrough: The Venus de Milo in the Louvre has lost both her arms; 'toplessly' plays on the statue's nudity.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venus de Milo statue famously lacks both upper limbs.

clue.text: Sport — Old English XI upset interpreter

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: In a sporting result, an Old English eleven suffers a defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges SPORT, O, E and XI; XI is a cricket or football team of eleven, and the letters are used as written.
explanation.definitionFit: One who explains or expounds a text is an expounder of its meaning.

clue.text: Carriage efficient and light

parts.note: port is an old word for bearing or deportment, one's carriage
able means competent, efficient

explanation.surface: A horse-drawn vehicle described as both efficient and lightweight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carriage' suggests a vehicle but here means how one carries oneself, PORT, as in deportment.
explanation.definitionFit: Something easily carried is lightweight enough to move about.

clue.text: Charity welcomed by palmist

explanation.surface: A fortune-teller gladly accepts donations.
explanation.walkthrough: A palmist reading hands is pleased when the client's hands are held out open.
explanation.definitionFit: Generosity in giving, and literally the state of having the palms spread open for reading.

clue.text: Comparatively dull circus job?

explanation.surface: Working in the big top is described as rather boring.
explanation.definitionFit: More docile or less exciting, and also a lion or animal trainer in the ring.

clue.text: And in one like Nash it goes to a woman's head

definitions.text: it goes to a woman's head

indicators.note: the word and sits inside the dandy, so one piece is put within the other

parts.note: Beau Nash was the famous Georgian dandy of Bath, so a beau is one like him
taken as written

explanation.surface: An elegant man like Nash wears something that ends up on a woman's head.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard 'Beau' Nash was an 18th-century leader of fashion in Bath; a beau is a fop or dandy.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow ribbon or band worn round the hair is a piece of headwear.

clue.text: Create new sort of game

indicators.note: a new sort of the word means its letters are given a fresh order

explanation.surface: Invent a novel type of game.
explanation.definitionFit: A French card game for two players.

clue.text: Spain in a spin suggests such fun

definitions.text: Spain in a spin suggests such fun

parts.words: Spain in a spin suggests such fun
parts.note: a whole nation whirling round is pictured as a nation taking part in a rustic folk dance

explanation.surface: A whirling Spain hints at some enjoyable activity.
explanation.walkthrough: Spain is a country, and a country spinning round is literally a nation dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: Traditional English folk dancing in sets and lines, read as a whole nation in motion.

clue.text: Get message over by display of arms

definitions.text: Get message over by display of arms

parts.words: Get message over by display of arms
parts.note: describes signalling with flags held in different arm positions, while sounding like a military show of force

explanation.surface: Make one's point by brandishing weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'display of arms' suggests weapons, but it means the signaller's arms holding flags.
explanation.definitionFit: A flag signalling system in which arm positions stand for letters.

clue.text: Married a girl providing heavenly food

parts.note: Anna is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A woman who weds provides divine nourishment.
explanation.definitionFit: The food sent from the sky to the Israelites in the wilderness.

clue.text: Mere wayward child this poet

indicators.note: wayward means straying from the path, so the letters go astray into a new order

parts.note: a son is a male child

explanation.surface: A naughty child is introduced as a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wayward' rearranges MERE into EMER; Ralph Waldo Emerson was the American poet and essayist.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Waldo Emerson, American essayist and writer of verse.

clue.text: Hard to starve anyway when food's brought home

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

indicators.note: anyway means in any manner at all, so the letters are arranged any old way

explanation.surface: It is difficult to go hungry at the season when crops are gathered in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anyway' is the anagram signal; 'when food's brought home' defines the season itself, not the act of gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: The season of gathering in the crops from the fields.

clue.text: Day's End, non-starter, like Loose Diamond

indicators.note: a non-starter here means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: sunset is the end of the day

explanation.surface: Reads like a list of racehorses: Day's End withdrawn, alongside Loose Diamond.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals suggest racehorse names; 'non-starter' takes the S off SUNSET.
explanation.definitionFit: A gem not yet fixed in a mount is loose.

clue.text: Competitor finally beaten

parts.note: describes the contestant who loses only at the last stage, in the final

explanation.surface: A rival is at last defeated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' suggests 'at last', but means beaten in the final.
explanation.definitionFit: The one who finishes second, defeated in the deciding round.

clue.text: Resort deep in Texas not as re-planned

indicators.note: something re-planned is laid out afresh, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: not means the word as is taken out of the word before it

explanation.surface: A holiday spot deep in Texas has been redesigned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not as' takes AS from TEXAS, leaving TEX; 'Resort' is the noun for a means to an end, not a holiday place.
explanation.definitionFit: A convenient means adopted to get out of difficulty, a measure of last recourse.

clue.text: State of one with no options

definitions.text: State of one with no options

parts.words: State of one with no options
parts.note: plays on the saying that those who ask for alms cannot be choosers

explanation.surface: A description of someone left without any choice.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'beggars can't be choosers' gives someone in this state no options.
explanation.definitionFit: Reduced to poverty, the condition of a mendicant, who proverbially cannot choose.

clue.text: In a sentence the prisoner's breakfast?

definitions.meaning: doing ... is British slang for serving a jail term

explanation.surface: A convict's morning meal described in terms of his prison term.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang 'porridge' means time in prison, from the oatmeal once served to inmates.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a prison term, and also oatmeal cooked in milk or water, eaten in the morning.

clue.text: Thirty-one day revolution

definitions.meaning: a month that has thirty-one days
the Russian uprising of 1917 named after its month

explanation.surface: A month-long uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: The tenth month has thirty-one days, and the 1917 Bolshevik uprising bears its name.

clue.text: Tricky step, one on a slippery slope

indicators.note: tricky means awkward or twisting, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An awkward step sends someone sliding down an icy incline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tricky' rearranges STEP with I mixed in.
explanation.definitionFit: A prepared ski run of packed snow is a slope one slides down.

clue.text: Bowler's target to get out quickly

definitions.meaning: a pin knocked down by a bowled ball in ninepins
in cricket, to dismiss batsmen in rapid succession

explanation.surface: A cricketer aims to dismiss batsmen in quick order.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, bowlers 'skittle out' a side when they dismiss its batsmen rapidly.
explanation.definitionFit: A pin knocked over in ninepins, and a verb for bowling out a team cheaply.

clue.text: No more champagne? Get away!

definitions.meaning: the cork flies and the bottle is empty, a playful sense
to leave suddenly, or informally to die

explanation.surface: The bubbly has run out, so clear off!
explanation.definitionFit: Literally the cork flying from a bottle, and slang for departing abruptly.

clue.text: Dismisses Peter at the S. African stopping-place

parts.note: outs means ousts or dismisses
Peter Pan, the boy who never grew up

explanation.surface: Peter is turned away at a South African resting spot.
explanation.walkthrough: In South Africa an outspan is a place where travellers unyoke oxen to rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Afrikaans term for a halting place where draught animals were unharnessed.

clue.text: Father meets uncle in Spain in open court

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
tio is Spanish for uncle

explanation.surface: Dad meets his Spanish uncle in an open courtyard.
explanation.definitionFit: A paved outdoor area or roofless inner courtyard, as in Spanish houses.

clue.text: May take a lot agreeing with the poll

definitions.meaning: a bidder at auction signals with the head to secure an item
poll is an old word for head, so this is assenting with the head

explanation.surface: Agreeing with an opinion survey may involve a lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poll' looks like a vote but is an old word for the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Bowing the head to bid for an auction lot, and to show assent.

clue.text: Alternative part in The Way of the World

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
a bit is a part

explanation.surface: A choice of role in Congreve's play 'The Way of the World'.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals suggest Congreve's comedy, but the def means the earth's path round the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: The path the earth travels round the sun.

clue.text: Local ghost, say, of the taxman?

indicators.note: say signals that the words are to be heard rather than spelled

parts.note: a local is a pub, an inn, and a ghost is a spectre

explanation.surface: A phantom in the neighbourhood, belonging to the tax collector?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' is British for one's nearby pub, INN; INN SPECTRE spoken sounds like the official title.
explanation.definitionFit: An official who examines tax returns, as in an inspector of taxes.

clue.text: Rough with flu spoilt one's leave

indicators.note: spoilt means ruined, so the letters are messed up into a new order

explanation.surface: A nasty bout of flu ruined someone's holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A leave of absence from duty, especially military.

clue.text: Be present at finish of a race

parts.note: the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
end means finish

explanation.surface: Turn up at the end of a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' reads backwards here: the finish comes after 'a race'. The TT is the Isle of Man motorcycle race.
explanation.definitionFit: To go to or be there at an event.
